Cyber Attack Disrupts Operations Across Egypt’s Real Estate Industry

Cairo—A sophisticated cyber attack has struck Egypt’s real estate industry, crippling the IT systems of several prominent property firms and bringing sales and project management processes to a standstill. The attack, which began late Monday night, is believed to be ransomware-related and remains ongoing, with affected companies struggling to regain access to critical data and digital platforms.

According to the Egyptian Real Estate Federation, at least seven major real estate agencies—including Nile Vista Properties and Pyramid Heights Developments—have reported being locked out of their internal networks. In a statement issued Tuesday morning, the Federation confirmed, “Multiple member firms are currently unable to access their databases, sales management tools, or client communications systems due to a malicious cyber intrusion.”

The disruption has forced the temporary closure of numerous real estate offices across Cairo, Giza, and Alexandria. “We arrived this morning to find our computers completely inaccessible, and we cannot process any property transactions or respond to client inquiries,” said Ahmed Samir, branch manager at Future Home Estates. “Our staff are doing their best to keep clients informed by phone, but most of our work relies on digital records and secure online platforms.”

On construction sites managed by affected real estate developers, digital project management tools are currently offline, causing delays in scheduling and on-site coordination. Workers at several new residential complexes in New Cairo and Sheikh Zayed City reported that site supervisors are resorting to manual methods to track progress and distribute daily tasks.

Industry analysts warn that the ongoing cyber attack could lead to significant financial losses if not resolved swiftly. “Most property sales, lease agreements, and project logistics in this sector are managed digitally. Extended downtime could seriously impact revenues and erode client trust,” said Reem El-Sayed, a Cairo-based real estate market analyst.

The Egyptian Real Estate Federation has urged all member firms to disconnect affected systems from the internet and seek professional cybersecurity assistance. The Federation’s spokesperson added, “Our priority is to safeguard sensitive client and company data while restoring normal operations as soon as possible.”

At the time of reporting, investigations are underway to determine the source of the attack, and there is no indication yet as to when the affected systems will be restored.
